name: POS terminal variants (layout family)
observed_behavior: The retail POS demo links distinct terminal pages pos.html and pos-2.html … pos-5.html from its index (252 unique links site-wide); further variants/pagination are enumerated in the route census (research/site-maps/). Sibling vertical demos (restaurant, pharmacy, laundry) are linked from the same index but are separate products, recorded as outbound references.
unverified_behavior: Checkout behaviour, payment/hardware integration, offline behaviour — template pages demonstrate layout, not processing.
business_problem: Different retail formats need different terminal layouts (grid density, cart position, category navigation).
jobs_to_be_done: Run a sale quickly by touch or keyboard; park/resume; refund; close the shift.
actions: Variant-specific (see interaction comparison in the S06 case study)
input_fields: Product search/scan, quantity, discount, tax, tender
states: Sale: open / parked / completed / refunded (proposed semantics)
audit: End-of-day reconciliation implied by reports routes (audit)
integrations: Barcode scanners, printers, payment terminals (hardware claims NOT_VERIFIED)
automation_candidates: Low-stock alert at sale time; parked-sale expiry
edge_cases: Offline queue conflicts; split tender rounding; duplicate submission on retry
security_privacy: Refunds require supervisor authorisation (proposed); full audit per drawer event
responsive_accessibility: Touch targets must be >=44px on terminal layouts; keyboard-first operation for scanner workflows
benefit_hypothesis: Layout variants let one POS engine serve multiple retail formats.
acceptance_criteria: Given a parked sale, when the cashier resumes it on another register, then totals and lines are identical.
